name: sled (Bw-tree-style embedded KV store)
baseline: RocksDB through rust-rocksdb 0.22 (the LSM-tree its README compares itself to), and SQLite through rusqlite
verdict_reason: sled claims LSM-like write speed with B+tree-like reads. Against an actual LSM, its batch writes were 1.9x slower than RocksDB and 2.4x slower than fjall, and its bulk load was the slowest tested. Its reads beat RocksDB but trail redb and LMDB. fjall's author excluded it from durable-write tests because it does not reliably fsync, and redb dropped it over open security advisories and no recent release.
tier_reason: Third-party benchmark (redb's author) with public source, pinned toolchain, and stated CPU and SSD.
claimed_speedup: Claimed: LSM-tree-like writes and B+tree-like reads. Measured (sled 0.34.7): batch writes 853 ms vs 451 ms RocksDB and 353 ms fjall; bulk load 24971 vs 13969 ms; random reads 1601 vs 2911 ms RocksDB but 1138 ms redb and 637 ms LMDB; uncompacted size 2.13 GiB vs 893.18 MiB.
workload: 5 million random 24-byte keys with 150-byte values: bulk load, 100 batches of 1,000, 1 million random reads, removals.
toolchain: rustc 1.89, sled 0.34.7, cargo bench release profile
platforms: Targets with std file I/O; Linux, macOS and Windows supported
one_liner: Lock-free embedded KV store whose LSM-like write claim fails: batch writes 1.9x slower than RocksDB, slowest bulk load tested.
how_it_is_fast: A lock-free tree over a log-structured page cache that writes page deltas instead of whole pages. In practice this gives decent reads but heavy space use and slower writes than real LSM engines.
use_it_when: Existing code already on sled 0.34 that is read-heavy and not durability-critical
skip_it_when: New projects: the stable 0.34.7 line dates from 2021 and 1.0 is still in alpha
Write-heavy workloads: RocksDB and fjall were faster
You need every acknowledged write to be on disk
caveats: Only one third-party run with sled in it (August 2025); redb has since removed sled from its comparison
sled's own claim of a billion operations per minute has no published harness or hardware
tradeoffs: The README itself says sled is beta, sometimes uses too much space, and points reliability-focused users to SQLite
On-disk format will change before 1.0 and need manual migration

evidence.quote: if reliability is your primary constraint, use SQLite. sled is beta.
if storage price performance is your primary constraint, use RocksDB. sled uses too much space sometimes.
| | redb | lmdb | rocksdb | sled | fjall | sqlite |
| uncompacted size | 4.00 GiB | 2.61 GiB | **893.18 MiB** | 2.13 GiB | 1000.95 MiB | 1.09 GiB |
Sled is not included because it does not reliably fsync
It has several security advisories open
